lead.headline: At least 68 people are killed when a high-speed train hits a stationary one south of Madrid, after passing a red signal
lead.short: At least 68 people were killed and dozens injured on Wednesday when a state-owned RENFE train ran into the back of a stopped IRYO train near Urda, about 120 km south of Madrid, on the Madrid-Seville line. Both trains were heading south. The transport minister said the RENFE train had been allowed to proceed despite a red signal.

why.text: It is one of Europe's deadliest rail crashes in years, on a high-speed network that many countries, India among them, look to as a model.

more: Transport minister Óscar Puente said a failure in the railway's computer communications system had stopped trains along a 63 km stretch, after which the operator ADIF took manual control. "There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed," he said. "It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances."

The RENFE train reportedly resumed at about 200 km/h before the collision, derailing carriages on both trains. Castilla-La Mancha's government said 58 people were in hospital, and a sports centre was turned into a treatment site. The union CSIF demanded Puente's resignation, accusing him of blaming a railway official, and Spain has begun three days of mourning.

seconds.headline: Alphabet loses nearly $400bn in value after a profit fall, as Microsoft beats forecasts and the Fed holds rates
seconds.short: Alphabet's shares fell about 10% after hours on Wednesday, wiping nearly $400bn off its value, after its quarterly profit fell 25% and it said heavy AI spending would continue. Microsoft rose about 3% as cloud revenue grew 30% and quarterly profit topped $36.6bn. The Fed held rates, though two members voted for a rise.

why.text: Big Tech's AI bills now move markets everywhere, India's IT shares included, and Amazon reports tonight.

more: "The reason why Alphabet is down is because their traditional revenue service of ad generation has been impacted by the very thing which is the AI boom," said Jamie Hannah of VanEck. Microsoft's quarterly revenue rose 19% to $92.3bn, days after it offered buyouts to about 60,000 staff, some of them in India.

Fed chair Kevin Warsh sounded more confident about inflation, but markets still price an 80% chance of a rise in December. Samsung's operating profit rose nearly ninefold to a record on AI chip demand, yet its shares fell more than 4%. In Mumbai the Sensex was up 0.9% at 2pm.

facts.Alphabet: down about 10% after hours, profit down 25%
facts.Fed: held; two members voted to raise

seconds.headline: Arnab's floods cut off about 2,000 people in Odisha's Ganjam, and the state plans to airlift villagers as Amit Shah calls the chief ministers
seconds.short: About 2,000 people are cut off by floodwater in Odisha's Ganjam district, Chief Secretary Anu Garg said on Thursday, and the state plans to airlift about 100 villagers first. More than 200 villages in 22 blocks of Ganjam and Gajapati are badly hit, and part of National Highway 326 has been washed away.

why.text: The storm has weakened, but its rain is now doing the damage, across Odisha and into Jharkhand.

more: Home minister Amit Shah has called the chief ministers of the affected states and promised all support. Indian Coast Guard helicopters are on standby, but rain and low cloud are holding back flights. The first airlifts are planned from Sanakhemundi, Asika and the Gopalpur area. Seventeen Odisha districts have had heavy rain, with Gajapati the worst hit.

Odisha moved 2,245 pregnant women to health centres before the storm, and 931 babies were born during it, The Hindu reports. Arnab crossed the Andhra coast on Wednesday as a very severe cyclonic storm and has since weakened into a depression. In Jharkhand, rain continues with orange alerts in six districts until Friday morning.

update.new: The floods after landfall: thousands cut off in Odisha.
update.front: The cyclone has passed, but the floods it left behind have cut off thousands and need an airlift.

seconds.headline: Apple unveils its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, with an OLED screen, from $2,899 and up to $14,549 fully loaded
seconds.short: Apple launched its first touchscreen MacBook Pros on Wednesday, with OLED displays, starting at $2,899. A fully loaded model with the top M5 Max chip, 128GB of memory and 16TB of storage costs $14,549, $4,400 more than the previous top 16-inch model. Preorders open on 30 October and the laptops go on sale on 6 November.

why.text: Apple held out against touchscreen laptops for years; now it has made one, and priced it for the AI-era memory shortage.

more: Both top models use the M5 Max chip, with an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU; the previous 16-inch MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149. The 14-inch top configuration costs $14,249. A 4TB drive adds $1,000, 8TB adds $3,000 and the new 16TB option $7,000; 128GB of memory adds $2,000, and nano-texture glass $150. TechCrunch blames part of the price on the memory shortage caused by AI's appetite for hardware.

It is nearly a decade since Apple tried the Touch Bar, which it later abandoned. Its new macOS shows different controls depending on whether the user last touched the screen or the trackpad. The cheaper M6 MacBook Pro and iMac launched a day earlier.

update.new: The touchscreen OLED models are out, with prices.
update.front: Apple's first touchscreen Mac, and a new price ceiling for a laptop.

seconds.headline: Real Madrid apologise to the Chinese people over Mbappé's remark, but China's state broadcaster keeps La Liga off air
seconds.short: Real Madrid apologised on Wednesday "to the Chinese people for any discomfort" caused by Kylian Mbappé's comment calling a figure in a meme "a Chinese dictator", after apologies from the player and La Liga. China Media Group, which runs CCTV, acknowledged the statement but has not resumed La Liga broadcasts, suspended since 26 October.

why.text: China is one of Madrid's and La Liga's biggest overseas markets, and the row is now costing both money.

more: "Our club maintains a deep respect for China, its history, its culture and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid," the club said, joining Mbappé's own apology. CMG has also dropped other matches and advertising featuring Mbappé.

The clip comes from an interview before Mbappé's appearance on the French podcast The Bridge in April 2025. Fans often edit his face onto images of dictators, and Thibaut Courtois has said the dressing room finds the memes hilarious. Goal says the storm is unlikely to blow over quickly. Three Chinese brands ended their deals with Mbappé on Tuesday.

update.new: The club apologises; China keeps La Liga off air.
update.front: The row has spread from one player to the club and the league, and Chinese television has pulled La Liga.

briefs.headline: Poland turns towards India after Donald Tusk's visit, the first by a Polish prime minister in 16 years
briefs.text: Better economic and defence ties are expected to follow, The Hindu reports, as Poland's strategic partnership with China develops cracks. Narendra Modi visited Poland in 2024, the first Indian prime minister to do so in 45 years.

update.new: After Tusk's visit, Poland is turning towards India.

briefs.headline: The Kerala High Court stops police from arresting a judge whose 17-year-old son drove the car in a fatal Kochi crash
briefs.text: The judge's son is 17. "The law has to be strictly followed," said Justice Kauser Edappagath, adding that the court could not bow to public opinion. The car hit a scooter at Cheranalloor on Sunday, killing Jayabalakrishnan, and the Kochi police chief has been moved.

briefs.text: Jairam Ramesh hit back after the prime minister mocked the Congress's showing. The BJP won six of 11 Uttar Pradesh council seats and all four in Karnataka, while the Congress beat it in Nagpur.

stories.headline: A round-the-world cruise ship halts in Cambodia over fuel costs, and its residents get eight hours to pack and leave
stories.short: The Villa Vie Odyssey, more than 750 days into a planned three-and-a-half-year voyage around the world, suspended operations in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, saying fuel costs had become unbearable since the Iran war began. About 200 passengers were told at 6am on Tuesday to leave by 2pm, eight hours later. The operator will spend 60 days restructuring.

why.text: It is a small, vivid sign of how the war's oil shock reaches ordinary lives far from the Gulf.

more: The US-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said the monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia had risen to as much as $8,000 from $1,800. It had slowed the itinerary and spent more time in port, but said passing the full increase to residents was "not a realistic solution", and that "no outcome is assured".

The nearly 200m ship, which can carry 650 passengers, left Belfast in October 2024 after months of delays for repairs, and planned to visit nearly 150 countries. Passengers Lanette Canen and Johan Bodin told the BBC they had known of the company's money troubles for some time.

briefs.headline: Israel's turnout reaches 77.7%, its highest since 1999, driven by Arab voters, as the count leaves no bloc with a majority
briefs.text: Turnout was 77.7%, the highest since 1999. With nearly 90% of votes counted there is still no clear winner. Channel 12 exit polls put Arab turnout near 80%, and Arab leader Jabareen says he could back an opposition-led government from outside it.

update.new: Record-high turnout, driven by Arab voters; still no majority.

briefs.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro, now in Miami, calls himself Brazil's rightful leader and says he did not flee, as Trump says 'we gave him a pass'
briefs.text: "I did not flee Brazil; I left for the sake of Brazil," he said, repeating unsupported fraud claims. Lula said "those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear". Reports say he left with decoys and a private jet, using an Italian passport.

update.new: Bolsonaro claims to be Brazil's leader; Trump says the US let him in.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms becomes India's second most valuable company, and its shares rise another 5% on the second day
stories.short: Jio Platforms closed its first day at ₹1,417, 27% above its issue price of ₹1,119, valuing it at about ₹12.5 lakh crore and ahead of Bharti Airtel, behind only its parent Reliance. On Thursday the shares rose another 5% to ₹1,482.70, more than 32% above the issue price. Mukesh Ambani was reported to have wept with joy.

why.text: India's biggest listing has passed its first test, which matters for the large share sales queuing behind it.

more: Nomura, Motilal Oswal and Elara Capital started coverage with Buy ratings, though their targets of ₹1,340 to ₹1,367 are below where the shares now trade. Nomura points to Jio's 41.7% share of India's wireless subscribers in August, data use per subscriber 27% higher than Airtel's and the lowest monthly churn, at 1.6%.

With most of its 5G spending done, Jio's capital spending is expected to fall to about 23% of revenue from 35%, freeing cash. Nomura also expects an industry-wide tariff rise of about 15% in November and December. Jio's IPO, of about ₹30,187 crore, was the largest in India's history.

update.new: Jio is now India's second most valuable company.

briefs.headline: Microsoft's voluntary exit offer extends to some teams in India, and one engineer says he was offered about ₹11 lakh to leave
briefs.text: One engineer said he was offered about ₹11 lakh to leave. The offer covers eligible staff in India, the US, Britain and Canada. More than 30% of those eligible took an earlier offer in July, Microsoft said; it has not said how many it expects to leave now.

stories.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon tops an independent AI index and leads on finding software flaws, but only security firms can use it
stories.short: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon on Wednesday, its latest frontier model, saying it makes significant gains in coding, agentic tasks and cybersecurity. It tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, and scores 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, which measures finding real-world bugs. For now only cybersecurity defence companies can use it.

why.text: AI is now finding software flaws faster than people can patch them, as the PHP crisis showed, and the labs are rationing their best models.

more: Carbon also leads ExploitGym, which measures how well a model turns a vulnerability into an exploit. Google says its teams have seen it "run for days to persist through dead ends" on complex engineering tasks, and that it resists prompt injection better and makes half as many unsupported claims as Argon, released earlier this month.

Access will widen later to other partners in Google's Fairwind programme. It will cost the same as Argon: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Separately, The Information reports that China's DeepSeek and Moonshot used outputs from GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models.

briefs.headline: The Rubin Observatory finds 2026 ED138, an icy object beyond Pluto that could be the sixth recognised dwarf planet
briefs.text: 2026 ED138 would become the sixth recognised dwarf planet if confirmed. It is between 600 and 1,500 km wide and orbits about 46 times as far from the Sun as Earth. Astronomers need more observations to confirm it is round enough to qualify.

briefs.headline: Djokovic comes from a set down to beat Humbert in Basel and keeps alive his hopes of a record 19th ATP Finals
briefs.text: The 39-year-old won 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in two and a half hours on his first visit to Basel in 15 years. He is chasing a 19th Finals appearance and is 11th in the race to Turin, where only the top eight qualify; Jannik Sinner has withdrawn with a knee problem.

briefs.text: Bayern won 6-1. Harry Kane was rested and got a guard of honour for his Ballon d'Or before 75,000 fans. Michael Olise scored twice, and assistant Aaron Danks ran the team.
